bites.title: Sight size
bites.body: Sight size is how ateliers have taught drawing since the 1800s: the model and your drawing sit side by side at the same size, so you can compare them directly, shape for shape, without doing math. Charles Bargue's drawing course (1860s, with Gerome) is the classic path: 197 plates, Van Gogh copied them. They're public domain.

bites.title: Load a plate
bites.body: Press a button below. You'll get a canvas with the plate on one side, blank paper on the other, exactly the same size, and your drawing layer (Copy) ready. Left-handed? Put the plate on the right so your hand never covers it: use the swap button, or tick Lefty layout in the Dojo once and every plate and pose follows.
bites.hint: No plates yet? Dojo tab > Public-domain library > Bargue drawing course plates > Download. Or type any pre-1930 artist into Find artist.

bites.title: A light grid
bites.body: Toggle the grid with {key:view_grid|Ctrl+Shift+'}. It helps you see where things land. Many ateliers frown on grids; use it to check, not to copy.

bites.title: Mark the extremes
bites.body: On the Copy layer, put four tiny ticks: the plate's top, bottom, far left and far right, transferred to your side. This is the box everything lives in.

bites.title: Plumb lines
bites.body: Grab the Line Tool from the toolbox and draw a straight vertical through a key point. What else sits on that line in the plate? Check yours.

bites.title: Near and far
bites.body: Window > New View on this same document, then Window > Tile. Zoom one view in for detail and keep the other fitted (2) to judge the whole. Like stepping back from the easel.

bites.title: Mirror check
bites.body: Flip with {key:mirror_canvas|M}. Errors jump out. Flip back when you've spotted one.

bites.title: 16 cleared
bites.body:
Plate left, paper right, same size, extremes, plumb lines, two views, mirror.

Now copy. Big shapes first, then smaller, then smaller.
